title: Payoff tables
objectives: Write a two-player game as a payoff table and read each player's best reply.

screens.title: Ben has chosen
screens.prose: Ana chooses a row and Ben a column. Each cell reads (Ana's payoff, Ben's payoff), in £. Suppose Ana hears Ben's column before she picks.
screens.question: For each column, tap the row Ana should play.

hints.text: Look down one column at a time, at the first numbers only.
Column L: Ana's first numbers are 3, 1 and 2.
U in column L, D in column C, M in column R.

feedback.correct: U against L, D against C and M against R: Ana's 3, 3 and 4.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. In each column, find the largest first number.

byKey.second: You picked the largest second number in each row. Those are Ben's payoffs; Ana reads the first number, down a column.

explain.text: Ana cannot change Ben's column, so she compares only the cells in it. In L she gets 3, 1 or 2, so U. In C the best is D (3) and in R it is M (4).

canvas.caption: Ana's best row in each column.

screens.title: Now Ben replies
screens.prose: The row you tapped in each column is Ana's **best reply** to that column. Now turn it round: Ana has chosen her row, and Ben hears it.
screens.question: For each row, tap the column Ben should play.

hints.text: Ben reads the second number in each cell, along a row.
Row U: Ben's numbers are 1, 2 and 4.
R against U, L against M, C against D.

feedback.correct: R against U, L against M and C against D: Ben's 4, 3 and 3.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Along each row, find the largest second number.

byKey.first: You tapped Ana's best replies again. Ben compares his own payoffs, the second numbers, along the row Ana chose.

explain.text: Ben's best reply to a row is the column with the largest second number in it. Against U that is R (4), against M it is L (3), against D it is C (3). One cell, (D, C), now wears both marks; lesson 3 names it.

canvas.caption: Ana's best replies and Ben's best replies.

screens.title: A story into a table
screens.prose: Two traders, Ana and Ben, each choose Buy now or Wait. If both buy, each makes £1. If one buys and one waits, the buyer makes £3 and the waiter £0. If both wait, each makes £2.
screens.question: Fill in each cell as Ana's payoff, then Ben's, such as 1, 1.

hints.text: Ana is the row, so her payoff comes first in every cell.
Ana buys and Ben waits: Ana is the buyer, so she makes £3 and he makes £0.
Buy row: 1, 1 and 3, 0. Wait row: 0, 3 and 2, 2.

feedback.correct: (1, 1) and (3, 0) in the Buy row; (0, 3) and (2, 2) in the Wait row.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Put Ana's payoff first, then Ben's, in every cell.

byKey.r0c2: In that cell Ana buys and Ben waits. The buyer makes £3, so it reads 3, 0.
byKey.r1c1: In that cell Ana waits and Ben buys. Ana makes £0 and Ben £3, so it reads 0, 3.

explain.text: Each cell is one pair of moves, with Ana's payoff first. The off-diagonal cells are mirror images: the buyer gets £3. A story becomes a table once every pair of moves has its two numbers.

screens.title: Best reply to Wait
screens.prose: Here is the buy-or-wait game as a table. Rows are Ana's moves and columns are Ben's, with (Ana's payoff, Ben's payoff) in £.
screens.question: Ben waits. What is Ana's best reply?

options.why: You picked the cell where both do well, (2, 2). Against Wait, Buy pays Ana £3, more than £2.
You compared Ana's 3 with Ben's 0. Compare Ana's two first numbers in the Wait column: 3 and 2.

hints.text: Look down the Wait column only.
Ana's first numbers there are 3 and 2.
3 is more than 2, so Buy.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare Ana's payoffs down the Wait column.

byKey.b: You chose the cell both like, (2, 2). Ana alone gains by buying: £3, not £2.

explain.text: In the Wait column Ana gets £3 by buying and £2 by waiting. So Buy is her best reply, although (Wait, Wait) pays both more than (Buy, Buy). Lesson 2 returns to that tension.

screens.title: Whose numbers?
screens.prose: Back to the first table. Ana has picked M, and Ben knows it.
screens.question: Tap Ben's best reply to M.

hints.text: Ben's payoff is the second number in each cell.
Ben's numbers are 3, 1 and 0, so L.

feedback.correct: L: Ben gets 3 there, against 1 and 0.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Read the second number in each cell of row M.

byKey.first: You read Ana's payoffs. Ben's are the second numbers.

explain.text: Row M holds (1, 3), (2, 1) and (4, 0). The 4 is Ana's, which Ben does not collect. His own numbers are 3, 1 and 0, so his best reply is L.

screens.title: A tie
screens.prose: A smaller game: Ana plays U or D, Ben plays L or R, payoffs (Ana, Ben) in £. Ana has picked U.
screens.question: Tap every best reply Ben has to U.

hints.text: Read Ben's numbers along row U.
Both cells give Ben 2.
A tie: both L and R are best replies.

feedback.correct: Both: Ben earns 2 with L and 2 with R.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare Ben's second numbers along row U.

byKey.just-r: You picked R, maybe for Ana's 3. Ben earns 2 in L too, so L is also a best reply.
byKey.just-l: L gives Ben 2, but so does R. A tie gives two best replies.

explain.text: Against U, Ben earns 2 in L and 2 in R. Neither beats the other, so both are best replies. A best reply is any move that does as well as the best, so there can be several.

screens.title: Reading any table
screens.prose:
Write $a_{ij}$ for Ana's payoff and $b_{ij}$ for Ben's in row $i$, column $j$. Ana's best reply to column $j$ maximises $a_{ij}$ down that column; Ben's to row $i$ maximises $b_{ij}$ along it.

$$\text{Ana: } \max_i a_{ij}, \qquad \text{Ben: } \max_j b_{ij}$$
screens.question: Ana wants her best reply to Ben's column C. Which numbers does she compare?

options.text: The first numbers down column C
The second numbers down column C
options.why: Those are Ben's payoffs. Ana collects the first number in each cell.

options.text: The first numbers along her own row
options.why: Along a row it is Ben's move that changes. Ana fixes the column and varies her row.

options.text: The total of each cell in column C
options.why: Ana keeps only her own payoff. Ben's share of a cell does not help her.

hints.text: Ben's column is fixed; Ana varies her row.
Varying the row means going down the column.
Her own payoffs, the first numbers, down column C.

feedback.correct: Down the column, first numbers only.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Fix Ben's column and compare Ana's own payoffs.

explain.text: Ana fixes Ben's column and moves her row, so she reads down it. She compares only her own numbers. Ben does the mirror image, along a row, with the second numbers.

screens.title: Drill
screens.prose: Three games, about three minutes each, as an interview allows. Say the reasoning aloud first. Two free resources hold more: the *Probability and Markets* guide and Open Yale Courses' *Game Theory* lectures. A trading firm wrote the guide about its own interviews. Zhou's green book and Crack's *Heard on the Street* hold a few game and betting questions.
screens.question: The 2 × 3 table is new; the 3 × 3 one opened this lesson. Fill in the four answers.

rows: 2 × 3 table: how many cells are Ana's best replies?
2 × 3 table: how many cells are Ben's best replies?
3 × 3 table: Ben plays L with chance 0.6 and R with 0.4. What is Ana's best row worth, in £?
Buy-or-wait game: Ana's best reply to both of Ben's moves, Buy or Wait?

hints.text: One best reply per column for Ana, one per row for Ben, when there are no ties.
For the beliefs, weight each row: $0.6 \times$ its L payoff $+ 0.4 \times$ its R payoff.
3 and 2; U is worth $0.6 \times 3 + 0.4 \times 2 = 2.6$; Buy.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Check the first answer that is marked.

byKey.r0c1: Check Ana's count: one best row in each of the three columns, T, B and B.
byKey.r1c1: Check Ben's count: one best column in each of the two rows, C and R.
byKey.r2c1: Weight each row by 0.6 and 0.4, not evenly: U gives $1.8 + 0.8 = 2.6$, M 2.2, D 1.6.
byKey.r3c1: Against Buy, Buy pays Ana £1 against £0; against Wait, £3 against £2.

explain.text: 2 × 3 table: Ana's best replies are T, B, B (3 cells) and Ben's are C, R (2 cells). With beliefs 0.6 and 0.4, U is worth 2.6, M 2.2 and D 1.6, so U. Buy beats Wait for Ana against either move: 1 > 0 and 3 > 2.

screens.title: Follow-up: quoting a spread
screens.prose: Two market makers each quote a spread of 1, 2 or 3 ticks. A client trades 100 lots with the tighter quote; a tie splits them 50 and 50. Each lot earns £1 per tick of spread. The interviewer asks about Ben quoting 3 ticks.
screens.question: Ben quotes 3 ticks. What is the most Ana can earn, in £?

hints.text: Fill column 3 first: work out each of Ana's quotes against Ben's 3 ticks.
Quoting 2 ticks, Ana is tighter and wins all 100 lots at 2 ticks each.
1 tick pays 100, 2 ticks pay 200, 3 ticks pay 150: so 2 ticks.

feedback.correct: £200, by quoting 2 ticks: 100 lots at 2 ticks.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out Ana's payoff for each of her three quotes against 3 ticks.

byKey.match: Matching at 3 ticks splits the flow: 50 lots at 3 ticks is £150. Undercutting by one tick wins all 100 lots.
byKey.tightest: One tick wins every lot but earns only £1 each. Two ticks still undercut Ben and earn £2 a lot.

explain.text: Against Ben's 3 ticks, Ana earns £100 at 1 tick, £200 at 2 ticks and £150 at 3 ticks. Her best reply is to undercut by one tick. A wide quote invites that undercut, which is what drives competing quotes tight.

canvas.caption: Column 3 filled in. Keep this table: lesson 3 comes back to it.

ideas: Ana picks the row and Ben the column; each cell holds (Ana's payoff, Ben's payoff).
Ana's best reply to a column is the row with the largest first number down that column.
Ben's best reply to a row is the column with the largest second number along it; ties give several.

formula.name: Best reply
formula.note: Down a column for Ana, along a row for Ben.

summary.trap: Reading Ana's number when Ben chooses. Ben collects the second number in each cell.

quiz.prose: Ana chooses the row and Ben the column. Each cell is (Ana's payoff, Ben's payoff), in £.
quiz.question: What is Ana's best reply to R?

options.why: You compared Ben's numbers in column R, 1 and 2. Ana's are the first numbers: 4 and 1.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the first numbers down column R.

explain.text: Down column R Ana gets 4 from T and 1 from B. So T is her best reply to R.

quiz.prose: The same table: (Ana's payoff, Ben's payoff), in £.
quiz.question: What is Ben's best reply to B?

options.why: You saw the 5 in (B, L). That is Ana's payoff; Ben gets 0 there.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Compare the second numbers along row B.

explain.text: Along row B Ben gets 0 from L and 2 from R. So R is his best reply to B.

quiz.prose: The same table. Ana thinks Ben plays L with chance 0.3 and R with chance 0.7.
quiz.question: What is row T worth to Ana on average, in £?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Weight T's payoff in each column by Ben's chance of playing it.

byKey.even: You averaged 2 and 4 evenly. R is likelier, so weight 4 by 0.7.
byKey.swap: You swapped the weights. L has chance 0.3, so it multiplies the 2.

explain.text: T pays 2 against L and 4 against R. Weighted: $0.6 + 2.8 = 3.4$. Row B is worth $1.5 + 0.7 = 2.2$, so T is Ana's best reply to this belief.

quiz.prose: A new table, (Ana's payoff, Ben's payoff) in £. Ben plays L.
quiz.question: How many best replies does Ana have to L?

feedback.correct: Two: U and M both give Ana 2.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Read Ana's first numbers down column L and look for ties.

byKey.one: U and M tie at 2. A tie gives Ana two best replies.

explain.text: Down column L Ana gets 2, 2 and 1. U and M tie for the best, so both are best replies. D, at 1, is not.
